title: CastillosBurstVEP100
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing a code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface task. The study introduces Burst c-VEP, a novel variant using short bursts of aperiodic visual flashes, and compares its performance to traditional m-sequence stimuli across two amplitude depths (100% and 40%). Data were acquired at 500 Hz using a 32-channel BrainProducts system and include 60 trials per subject with convolutional neural network-based classification achieving 95.6% accuracy.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 12 healthy participants (mean age 30.6±7.1 years) at 500 Hz using a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system with standard 10-20 montage and active electrodes. Participants performed a 4-class c-VEP target selection task in a factorial design manipulating pattern type (burst vs m-sequence) and amplitude depth (100% vs 40%). Visual stimuli were presented on a 60 Hz Dell monitor using PsychoPy. Burst codes consisted of brief flashes (~50ms) with minimum 200ms inter-burst intervals. EEG was decoded using a CNN architecture with spatial (8×1, 16 filters), temporal (1×32, 8 filters), and 2D convolution (5×5, 4 filters) layers applied to 250ms sliding windows with 2ms stride. Classification employed sequential train/test splits with Pearson correlation for target selection.
